repollo.title: Roasted cabbage with miso and lemon butter
repollo.summary: Roasted cabbage wedges with golden edges and tender centres, finished with white miso and lemon butter. An easy oven side with plenty of savoury flavour.
repollo.notes: Keep a piece of core in each wedge so it holds together. Taste before adding salt: miso is already salty. Contains milk and soy; check miso for gluten-containing grains. Refrigerate covered at 4 °C or below for up to 3 days and reheat thoroughly. Oven times vary with wedge size.
steps: Cut the cabbage
Preheat a conventional oven to 220 °C. Remove damaged leaves and cut 800 g trimmed cabbage into 8 wedges, keeping a piece of core in each.
Dry and arrange
Dry the wedges and arrange on a metal tray about 30 × 40 cm. Brush the cut faces with 20 g oil, leaving space between them.
Roast the first side
Roast for 20 minutes with one cut face against the tray, until the edges begin to brown.
Turn and soften
Turn with a spatula. Add 40 ml water to the tray, cover with foil and roast for 15 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the centre.
Mix the butter
Meanwhile, mix 35 g softened butter with 25 g white miso, 20 g lemon juice and 5 g grated garlic.
Brush the wedges
Carefully remove the foil, avoiding the steam. Spread the miso butter over the upper faces of all 8 wedges.
Finish browning
Roast uncovered for another 5 minutes, watching so the miso colours lightly without burning. If the core is still firm, extend the covered stage before adding the butter.
Serve with sesame
Transfer to a platter and scatter over 5 g toasted sesame seeds. Serve 2 wedges per person with the tray juices.
faq: Can I use red miso?
It tastes stronger and is often saltier. This recipe uses white miso; start with less if using another type and adjust to taste.
Why keep some core?
It holds the leaves together when turning. It should be tender when pierced before serving.
How do I stop the miso burning?
Add the butter only at the end and watch the final 5 minutes of roasting.

arroz.title: Crispy rice salad with chickpeas and cucumber
arroz.summary: Oven-crisped rice with chickpeas, cucumber, carrot and lemon tahini dressing. Toss just before serving to keep the rice crunchy and the vegetables fresh.
arroz.notes: Use cooked rice cooled quickly and refrigerated within 1 hour; use within 24 hours. Do not use rice left at room temperature for hours. The recipe starts with cooked, cold rice; its earlier cooking and chilling time is not included. Contains sesame and soy; check soy sauce if avoiding gluten. Store components separately and dress only what you will eat.
steps: Separate the rice
Preheat a conventional oven to 210 °C. Loosen 400 g properly refrigerated cooked, cold rice with a fork.
Spread on the tray
Toss rice with 20 g oil and 15 g soy sauce. Spread thinly on a parchment-lined metal tray about 30 × 40 cm.
Bake and stir
Bake for 20 minutes, stir and spread out again. Bake another 10–15 minutes, watching towards the end, until golden and crisp.
Prepare the vegetables
Wash 250 g cucumber and 100 g carrot. Slice cucumber into half-moons and grate the carrot. Dry cucumber well so it does not soften the rice.
Drain the chickpeas
Rinse and drain 300 g cooked chickpeas. Pat dry with kitchen paper and chop 15 g parsley.
Whisk the dressing
Mix 35 g tahini, 35 g lemon juice, 30 ml water and the remaining 10 g oil. Whisk until smooth and pourable.
Combine the base
Let rice cool on the tray for 5 minutes. In a wide bowl, combine chickpeas, cucumber, carrot and parsley separately.
Add the crunch and serve
Add rice and dressing just before eating. Toss briefly and divide between 4 plates. Serve promptly: the assembled salad loses its crunch.
faq: Can I use freshly cooked rice?
Wet rice needs drying first and gives a different result. This recipe uses cold rice that has been cooled and refrigerated correctly.
Can I make it ahead?
Prepare the components separately and add rice and dressing at serving time. The mixed salad softens.
How can I adjust the dressing?
Tahini thickness varies. Add water gradually if needed until it falls from a spoon without becoming watery.

coliflor.title: Crispy baked cauliflower with hot honey
coliflor.summary: Cauliflower bites in a thin batter and panko coating, baked until golden. Add the chilli and lemon honey at the end to help preserve the crisp surface.
coliflor.notes: Cut florets about 4 cm across and leave space between them. Nutrition includes all the batter and crumbs; actual values are lower if some remain unused. Contains wheat; check panko labels. Heat varies with the chilli. Honey is unsuitable for babies under 12 months. Serve freshly baked; storage softens the coating and leftovers can be reheated in the oven.
steps: Cut and dry
Preheat a conventional oven to 220 °C. Wash and thoroughly dry 600 g trimmed cauliflower, cut into florets about 4 cm across.
Make the batter
Whisk 70 g flour with 110 ml water, 3 g sweet paprika and 3 g salt. The flowing batter should coat the cauliflower lightly.
Coat the florets
Dip florets in the batter and let excess drip into the bowl. Distribute batter over all pieces, avoiding thick clumps.
Add panko
Put 80 g panko in a shallow dish and press each floret gently into the crumbs to coat all sides.
Arrange and oil
Space pieces on a large parchment-lined baking tray. Drizzle 25 g oil thinly over them without piling them up.
Bake until golden
Bake for 15 minutes, carefully turn and bake another 10–15 minutes, until panko is golden and a knife enters the stalk easily.
Mix the hot honey
Mix 45 g honey with 1 g chilli flakes and 15 g lemon juice. If very thick, warm gently without boiling.
Glaze and serve
Transfer hot cauliflower to a platter and drizzle thinly with hot honey immediately before eating. Serve at once, collecting the remaining sauce from the platter.
faq: Does the honey go in the oven?
No. Add it at the end so it does not burn or soak the coating while cooking.
Can I use fine breadcrumbs?
Yes, but the surface will be less airy and browning time may differ. This version uses panko.
Why is it not crisp?
Surface water, crowded pieces and too much batter hinder browning. Dry well and leave space between pieces.
coliflor.serving_size: one quarter of the cauliflower and sauce

gyozas.title: One-dish coconut curry gyoza bake
gyozas.summary: Frozen vegetable gyoza heated in coconut milk, red curry and spinach sauce. A one-dish dinner with tender wrappers and plenty of sauce to spoon up.
gyozas.notes: Use commercially prepared, fully precooked vegetable gyoza suitable for reheating, not raw meat or seafood dumplings. Follow the packet if it requires longer cooking. Curry paste may contain shellfish; choose one without it to keep the recipe plant-based. Contains wheat and soy; check all labels for other allergens. Follow the manufacturer's storage and reheating instructions; if reheating is prohibited, serve freshly cooked and do not save for reheating.
steps: Prepare the dish
Preheat a conventional oven to 200 °C. Use a baking dish about 30 × 22 cm and at least 5 cm deep.
Mix the sauce
Whisk 400 g coconut milk, 150 ml water, 25 g red curry paste, 15 g soy sauce, 10 g ginger and 5 g garlic directly in the dish.
Add spinach
Wash and thoroughly drain 120 g spinach. Spread over the sauce and press down lightly to moisten.
Arrange the gyoza
Arrange 600 g fully precooked vegetable gyoza in one layer, still frozen. Submerge their bases in sauce and leave the upper pleats visible.
Bake covered
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 25 minutes. The sauce should heat and create steam to soften the wrappers.
Uncover and check
Carefully remove foil and bake another 10 minutes. Check that a gyoza's centre reaches 74 °C; follow any longer packet timing. If still cold, cover and continue in 5-minute intervals.
Finish with lime
Remove from the oven and stir 25 g lime juice into the sauce without breaking the gyoza. Thinly slice 20 g spring onion.
Divide and serve
Divide gyoza, spinach and sauce between 4 deep plates. Add spring onion and serve hot. The sauce stays fluid rather than forming a gratin.
faq: Can I use raw gyoza?
This recipe uses fully precooked vegetable gyoza. Raw dumplings, especially meat or seafood ones, require their manufacturer's specific cooking instructions.
Can I use coconut drink instead?
Not directly: it is much more diluted. Use unsweetened culinary canned coconut milk.
Can I reduce the heat?
Yes. Pastes vary in strength; start with less curry and adjust. Nutrition is calculated using the stated 25 g.
gyozas.serving_size: one quarter of the gyoza, spinach and sauce

yogur.title: No-bake yogurt, biscuit and strawberry cups
yogur.summary: Thick Greek yogurt and biscuits soften together overnight, then get a fresh strawberry topping. A three-ingredient spoon dessert inspired by viral yogurt cups.
yogur.notes: Use thick plain full-fat Greek yogurt, not drinking yogurt. Biscuits provide the sweetness; the result retains yogurt's tang and is not intended to be unmoulded. Contains milk and wheat; check biscuits for egg or other allergens. Keep covered at 4 °C or below for up to 2 days and add strawberries at serving time. Total time includes 8 hours of refrigeration.
ingredients: thick plain full-fat unsweetened Greek yogurt
steps: Prepare the glasses
Set out 4 clean glasses of about 250 ml and a spoon. Keep 600 g Greek yogurt chilled until assembling.
Break the biscuits
Divide 120 g biscuits into 4 portions of 30 g. Break into 2–3 cm pieces without crushing to powder.
Make the first layer
Spoon 75 g yogurt into each glass and gently smooth. This uses half the yogurt.
Add the first biscuits
Distribute 15 g broken biscuit over the yogurt in each glass. Press lightly to make contact with the yogurt.
Finish the layers
Add the remaining 75 g yogurt per glass. Tuck in the other 15 g biscuit from each portion and push the pieces under the yogurt until fully covered.
Cover and chill
Cover all 4 glasses without pressing the surface down. Refrigerate at 4 °C or below for 8 hours to hydrate and soften the biscuits.
Prepare strawberries
Just before serving, wash and dry 200 g strawberries, remove hulls and cut into pieces. Do not add wet fruit to the glasses.
Top and serve
Uncover and add 50 g strawberries to each glass. Serve cold with a spoon, showing the softened yogurt and biscuit layers.
faq: Is this Japanese cheesecake?
No. It is a yogurt and biscuit dessert inspired by a social trend, not baked Japanese cheesecake or a cake containing cheese.
Can I use drinking yogurt?
It will not have the same consistency. Thick Greek yogurt is needed for a spoon dessert rather than a drink.
Can I eat it before 8 hours?
Yes, but parts of the biscuit will still be firm. The stated rest aims for a soft, even texture.
